symptom: mendixlabs/mxcli#1284: on Windows `mxcli test --attach` always says the app that published `.mxcli/test-endpoint.json` "is no longer running" although the pid is alive; the dev loop's `run-local.json` "already serving" detection never fires either
cause: pid liveness was `os.FindProcess(pid)` + `Signal(0)`; Go supports no signal but Kill on Windows and returns EWINDOWS for the rest, so every pid read dead
insight: The correct Windows check (OpenProcess(SYNCHRONIZE) + WaitForSingleObject(h, 0) == WAIT_TIMEOUT) already existed in docker/procgroup_windows.go since the waitReady incident, but two pid-based copies of the Signal(0) idiom were written separately and never moved over; Linux-only CI could not see it. Four tests were already red on a native Windows run (TestHandshakeRoundTrip, TestAttachUsesTheAdminPasswordNotTheEndpointToken, TestDevLoopHandshake_RoundTrip, TestWarnIfDevLoopServing_FiresForALiveDevLoop). Grep for `Signal(syscall.Signal(0))` / `Signal(0)` before trusting any new liveness check; use procalive.Alive for a bare pid.
